recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #13 - Deploying to Netlify
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough on deploying an Astro site to Netlify by connecting a GitHub repository. Covers creating a GitHub repo, pushing local commits, linking the repo to Netlify, configuring build settings, and triggering an automatic deployment.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #12 - Client Islands (React)
recent_posts.summary: A practical introduction to Astro's island architecture, explaining how to add interactive client-side components to otherwise static Astro pages. Covers installing the React integration via `npx astro add react`, creating a React component with useState, importing it into an Astro page, and using client directives (`client:load` vs `client:visible`) to control when JavaScript is hydrated in the browser. Demonstrates lazy hydration with `client:visible` so JavaScript only loads when the component scrolls into view.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #11 - Server Side Rendering
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial covering how to enable server-side rendering (SSR) in Astro by adding a server adapter and using the `export const prerender = false` directive. Explains when SSR is preferable over static site generation, such as for frequently changing data or user-specific pages. Demonstrates installing the Netlify adapter, marking a page as on-demand rendered, and fetching live data from an API endpoint on each request.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #10 - Dynamic Routes
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial covering how to implement dynamic routes in Astro using the `getStaticPaths` function. It walks through creating a file-based dynamic route with square bracket syntax (e.g., `[id].astro`), fetching a content collection, mapping books to static page params and props, and rendering markdown content using Astro's `render` function and the Content component.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #9 - Content Collections (with Markdown)
recent_posts.summary: This tutorial covers how to use Astro's content collections with markdown files instead of a single JSON file. It walks through restructuring a book review site's data source by switching from the `file` loader to the `glob` loader, organizing markdown files in a subfolder, using front matter for metadata, and leveraging auto-generated IDs from filenames. The lesson also shows how to use those IDs as dynamic hrefs in a book card component.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #8 - Content Collections (with JSON)
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough of Astro's content collections feature using JSON as a data source. Covers setting up a content.config.ts file, defining a collection with the file loader, adding a Zod schema for type safety and IntelliSense, querying data with getCollection(), and updating component props to use the CollectionEntry type. Also demonstrates accessing nested data properties and rendering rating and summary fields in a book card component.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #7 - Reusable Components
recent_posts.summary: A beginner tutorial on creating reusable components in Astro. Covers extracting a BookCard template into its own .astro component file, passing data via props, destructuring props using Astro.props, and defining a TypeScript Props interface to enforce type safety and enable IntelliSense in the component template.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #6 - Outputting Lists
recent_posts.summary: A beginner tutorial on rendering lists of data in Astro using Front Matter and the array map method. Covers defining a TypeScript interface for book data, mapping over an array to output templated HTML for each item, and conditionally displaying a message when the list is empty. Also highlights key differences from React, such as no need for a key prop and support for multiple root elements per list item.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #5 - Templating
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of Astro component templating, covering the front matter section for writing JavaScript/TypeScript that runs only at build time or on the server. Demonstrates defining variables, using objects, and outputting values in templates with curly brace syntax. Also covers conditional rendering using logical AND expressions to show or hide content based on whether a user is logged in, with a simulated random user function to illustrate the pattern during development.

recent_posts.title: Astro Crash Course #4 - Styles
recent_posts.summary: A beginner tutorial on adding styles to an Astro project. Covers multiple approaches including inline style tags, external stylesheets, and Tailwind, then focuses on component-scoped styles. Explains how Astro scopes styles by default using data attributes, how to override this with the `is:global` directive for site-wide styles, and how to mix scoped and global styles within a layout component. Ends with a practical example applying both global and page-specific styles across a multi-page site.

top_posts.title: HTMX Tutorial for Beginners #1 - What is HTMX?
top_posts.summary: HTMX is a JavaScript library for creating dynamic web applications using a hypermedia-driven approach. It extends HTML's hypermedia controls, enabling interactions with the server through simple attributes without extensive client-side JavaScript. The tutorial introduces HTMX, compares it to other frameworks like React, and sets the stage for building a reading list application using Node.js and Express for the backend.

top_posts.title: Complete React Native Tutorial #1 - Introduction & Setup (Expo)
top_posts.summary: React Native is a cross-platform framework that allows you to build applications for iOS, Android, and the web with a single codebase using JavaScript or TypeScript and React components. It translates these components into native elements for mobile platforms. This tutorial guides you through setting up a React Native project using Expo, targeting iOS and Android devices, and explains how to preview the app on a real device with Expo Go. The tutorial includes setting up basic component templates and configuring a development environment for a seamless coding experience.

top_posts.title: HTMX Tutorial for Beginners #3 - GET Requests (hx-get)
top_posts.summary: Learn how to enhance your web application using HTMX by adding a button that sends a GET request to the server to fetch and dynamically display a list of books. The tutorial covers creating the button, handling the request on the backend, and rendering the response into the HTML page without additional JavaScript.

top_posts.title: Laravel for Beginners #1 - Introduction & Setup
top_posts.summary: Welcome to an introductory guide to Laravel, a modern PHP framework for web development. This series will teach you from the ground up to create a small CRUD application. You will learn about fundamental Laravel concepts like routing, views, models, data migrations, and more. The tutorial starts with setting up your development environment using a tool called Her, which simplifies the setup process. By the end of this series, you'll have a functional Laravel application and a deeper understanding of its core components.

top_posts.title: Complete React Native Tutorial #12 - Backend Setup with Appwrite
top_posts.summary: Learn how to set up a backend for a React Native application using Appwrite, a backend-as-a-service platform. This tutorial covers creating an Appwrite account, setting up a project, registering a platform, and integrating the backend services like authentication and database into a React Native app.
